body_ar:
حكم خياطة الرقيق من الثياب.
الحمد لله والصلاة والسلام على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم تسليماً كثيراً. أما بعد: فأقول للأخوات: إن ما تقدمن به من الأسئلة بين يدي، وما لا أعلمه فسيكون الجواب فيه بلا أدري، وما أعلمه أيضاً فإنما الإفتاء فيه من باب قول الشاعر: لعمر أبيك ما نسب المعلا إلى كرم وفي الدنيا كريم ولكن البلاد إذا اقشعرت وصوح نبتها رعي الهشيم./
السؤال: هل يجوز لشخص عنده عيال خياطة الرقيق من الثياب مع العلم أنه محتاج إلى ثمنه ولا يوجد سوى الرقيق يخيطه؟.
الجواب: ورد عن عمرو بن مرة أنه جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: (يا رسول الله! حرمت فما أُراني أرزق إلا من دفي بكفي فهل تأذن لي في ذلك؟ فقال: لا آذن لك ولا كرامة، ولو كنت تقدمت إليك لأوجعتك ضرباً ولحلقت رأسك مثلة، ولأبحت مالك لأهل المدينة)، فإن الله عز وجل قد وسع في الأرزاق من الحلال، ووسع السبل إلى ذلك، ومن أراد أن يوسع الله عليه في رزقه فلا يعمد إلى ما حرم الله عليه، فإن خياطة الرقيق من الثياب وبيعه لمن يستعمله استعمالاً لا يجوز من التعاون على الإثم والعدوان الذي نهى الله عنه. ...
body_en:
## The ruling on sewing sheer garments

Praise belongs to God, and blessing and peace upon the Messenger of God, God bless him and his family and his Companions and grant them abundant peace. To proceed: I say to the sisters that the questions you have put are before me. What I do not know, the answer to it will be "I do not know"; and as for what I do know, giving a considered legal opinion (fatwā) on it falls under the poet's words:

*By your father's life, al-Muʿallā was never ascribed generosity while there was a generous man in the world; but when the lands turn bleak and their herbage withers away, then the dry stubble is grazed.*

**The question:** Is it permissible for a person who has dependents to sew sheer garments, given that he needs the price of them and there is nothing but the sheer kind for him to sew?

**The answer:** It has come from Amr ibn Murrah that he came to the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "Messenger of God, I have been deprived, and I do not see myself provided for except from my tambourine with my hand — will you permit me that?" He said: "I will not permit you, and no honour to you. Had I come to you beforehand, I would have beaten you painfully, and shaved your head as a disfigurement, and declared your property free to the people of Medina."

For God, mighty and majestic, has made provision ample from what is lawful, and has made the ways to it ample. Whoever wishes God to make his provision ample for him, let him not resort to what God has forbidden him. For sewing sheer garments, and selling them to one who will use them in a way that is not permissible, is part of cooperating in sin and transgression, which God has forbidden. …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis after the first question of a sitting explicitly described as having many, since the Sheikh's own preamble says the sisters' questions are before him. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/d-a-97.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: ورد عن عمرو بن مرة أنه جاء إلى رسول الله ... فقال: لا آذن لك ولا كرامة، ولو كنت تقدمت إليك لأوجعتك ضرباً ولحلقت رأسك مثلة، ولأبحت مالك لأهل المدينة
flags.context: the report the Sheikh cites in support of the answer
options: keep the citation exactly as given, with no collection and no grading, and obtain a grading before publication
supply the collection and the grading from the literature
omit the report and keep the reasoning
flags.note: The highest-risk single passage in this slice. The Sheikh introduces the report with 'ورد عن' — 'it has come from' — which is the weakest of the citation formulas and asserts nothing about its standing. He names no collection, no chain and no grading. Style guide section 4 forbids adding a grading he did not give, so the English adds none. But the content is severe — a threatened beating, a punitive shaving of the head and the declaring of a man's property free to be taken — and an English page carrying it under the Sheikh's name, with no grading beside it, will be read as his endorsement of that severity and will travel. This record must not be published until the Sheikh's office supplies the grading he holds the report to have. Style guide section 12 applies in full. Note also that the report is about a man earning from a tambourine, not about sewing, and is cited as an analogy for earning from what is impermissible.

flags.arabic: خياطة الرقيق من الثياب وبيعه لمن يستعمله استعمالاً لا يجوز من التعاون على الإثم والعدوان
options: is part of cooperating in sin and transgression, which God has forbidden
amounts to helping in sin and so is not allowed
flags.note: The operative ruling, and it must be rendered at exactly the strength the Arabic gives it — no more. The Sheikh does not say the act is forbidden (ḥarām). He says it falls under cooperating in sin and transgression, which God forbade; the prohibition attaches to the category, and he leaves the reader to draw the inference. He also qualifies it twice, and both qualifications must survive: the garments are sold 'to one who will use them in a way that is not permissible', and it is the selling as well as the sewing that is at issue. Writing 'sewing sheer garments is forbidden' would strip both qualifications and state a wider ruling than the one given. Note too that the questioner's circumstances — dependents, need, no other work available — are put to the Sheikh and are not addressed in the served text, which breaks off immediately after this sentence.

'يجوز' is the verb of 'جائز', which in a question of this kind asks after the ruling of permissibility. Note that the same verb appears later in the answer in 'استعمالاً لا يجوز', where it qualifies the buyer's use and not the tailor's act; the English keeps 'permissible' in both places so the reader can see that the Sheikh's answer turns on the second use of the word.

'رقيق' of cloth is thin to the point of showing what is beneath. 'Sheer' carries that in English without the clinical register of 'diaphanous' or the neutrality of 'thin', and the answer's whole reasoning depends on the garment being see-through. Note that 'رقيق' is also the word for a slave, an unrelated homonym that a reader of the Arabic alone might trip on.

flags.arabic: لعمر أبيك ما نسب المعلا إلى كرم وفي الدنيا كريم / ولكن البلاد إذا اقشعرت وصوح نبتها رعي الهشيم
flags.context: the verses in the Sheikh's own preamble
options: rendered as prose in italics, as a formula of self-deprecation
rendered literally with al-Muʿallā left unexplained
flags.note: The lines do real work and should not be cut. The Sheikh applies them to himself: al-Muʿallā was called generous only because no truly generous man was left, as dry stubble is grazed only when the pasture has failed — so he answers only because better authorities are not to hand. Rendered as prose in italics per style guide section 4, with no rhymed English attempted. 'المعلا' is a proper name and is left unexplained, as the Sheikh leaves it.

flags.arabic: وما لا أعلمه فسيكون الجواب فيه بلا أدري
options: What I do not know, the answer to it will be 'I do not know'
Whatever I do not know, my answer will be that I do not know
flags.note: Recorded not because the rendering is doubtful but because the sentence is the Sheikh's own statement of method and should be visible in the English at full strength. He states, before any question is put, that he will decline questions he cannot answer. It bears directly on how the rest of the corpus is to be read.

translator_notes: One of three records, IDs 722-724, filed in the written-fatwa section and uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about half an hour of one another. Unlike most of that section, each of the three carries a real written question and a real written answer, and none is a title-only stub. All three are nonetheless excerpts: each breaks off after the first question and the full sitting sits behind a .doc or .docx download in the /medias/doc/d-a-* series.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The record's title names a sitting of women's questions, and the Sheikh's preamble addresses 'the sisters'; the one question served concerns a tailor with dependents. This is not a title/body mismatch of the kind flagged at record 397 elsewhere in the corpus — it is the first question of a general sitting — but a reader should be told that the title describes the sitting and not the question.
The record has no site synopsis. The heading is the site's editorial label for the question; everything from 'Praise belongs to God' onward is the Sheikh's own words and the questioner's.

'مثلة' is rendered 'as a disfigurement'; it is the technical term for punitive mutilation, and the English keeps it as the source's own characterisation of the act rather than softening it to 'as a punishment'.
The source closes with a space before the ellipsis and with the ellipsis set off from the preceding sentence; reproduced as served.
